families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

meaning: Each tie is a pointer that landed. Whether the paper and the Lean say the same thing is a reading.

rows.fidelity_note: The final condition has fifteen clauses, and each clause constrains one or more of the shared data choices. This is the proposed reading order.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The cell data include the steady certificate data in full and add the cell-specific quantities. Counting the inherited information separately agrees with this definition.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.FracCellData

rows.fidelity_note: The steady certificate data have 46 directly specified quantities, including profiles, forcing, constraints, rows, bounds and adjoints. The numerical count in the sentence agrees with the source.
rows.name: Breakdown.SteadyCert.FracCertData

rows.fidelity_note: The fifteen clauses concern the same certificate, field instances, cell calculations, tree, assembly, constants and reduction data. In particular, the existential tree and enclosure choices must keep their stated common scope.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The displayed theorem states both whole-space and torus breakdown under the full cell condition. The readable statement file leaves its proof to the corresponding implementation; its conclusion remains conditional.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpaceAndTorus_of_cell_system_condition

rows.fidelity_note: The first condition combines field instances, valid cells, local calculations, a common matrix tree, pairing errors, shape witnesses and the fixed constants. The table correctly describes its role rather than claiming a numerical instance.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The second condition requires positive periods throughout K, positive constant weight and the stated closure and inclusion properties of the bounding harmonic sets.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The third condition simultaneously requires the local forms, all compatible row vectors, mode and exterior coverage, elimination bounds and tree identifications for the chosen data.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The enclosure bounds must hold for every parameter in K with the particular three constants used in the top-level coercivity formula. Existence of other enclosure constants is insufficient.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The first scalar coercivity bound is the square root of the multiplier-bound expression divided by the square root of 3/50, and it must not exceed c₁. This is the first inequality of (B.22).
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The condition is c₂ ≥ √(1000·50/3), exactly the pinning lower bound in (B.22).
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The seventh condition includes all residual bounds, three smallness inequalities, invertibility of the frame, parameter inclusion and a strict nonzero-profile bound. These are the roles listed in the table.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The eighth condition identifies the approximate profile, pressure gradient and selected adjoints with the specified shape formulas, including the pin-target identity.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The ninth condition requires the affine frequency and multiplier identities, all constant, linear and quadratic pairing enclosures, the exterior norm bounds and the exact total offset of (B.59).
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The central error is controlled in the supremum and gradient L² norms, and the parameter variation in the supremum and gradient L³ norms. Their two stated combinations bound the convection gap and form shift.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: This condition bounds the frozen reference form by a lower strain bound and a gradient L³ bound. The profile-shift estimates belong to the preceding condition and are added later in Lemma B.9.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: For each selected adjoint, the condition allows either a uniform L³ bound with coefficient 2/(√3 w*) or a uniform L² bound with coefficient c_w/√w*. This is the alternative in Lemma B.10.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The field, coupling coefficients, central profile, parameter directions and reciprocal-period coefficients must agree with the reduction data. The fitted-direction set is required to be empty.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The potential representations and compact pin generators must satisfy their validity conditions and equal the fields used in the defect estimate.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: Every selected adjoint must satisfy the potential norms, dual remainder bounds, parameter-direction estimates and pin-error budget culminating in (B.53).
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: In the surrounding table, n is the number of parameter and constraint coordinates. The linked cell data keep that dimension separate from the symmetry order κ and the azimuthal frequency κι₁.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData

rows.fidelity_note: The data contain a natural-number symmetry order without fixing its value. The lower bound is imposed by the separate cell hypothesis, consistently with the sentence.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData

rows.fidelity_note: The cell hypothesis requires κ ≥ 3. It does not specialise κ to the numerical example 19 described in Appendix C.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellHypothesis

rows.fidelity_note: The temporal index is exactly 2ι₂ − ι₁, the coefficient of 2πθ in (B.2).
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime

rows.fidelity_note: The azimuthal index is exactly κι₁, the coefficient of φ in (B.2).
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth

rows.fidelity_note: The condition is f(θ+1,y)=f(θ,y) for every θ and y. It uses the normalised time of period one.
rows.name: Breakdown.IsTimePeriodic

rows.fidelity_note: The cylindrical radius is √(y₁²+y₂²). This is the radial coordinate of a meridian cell, distinct from |y| in the compactified chart.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylRadius

rows.fidelity_note: The gradient entries are selected in row order from the first nine coordinates. The formula imposes no symmetry on that 3 by 3 array; the remaining coordinates are available for velocity.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.gradOf

rows.fidelity_note: The tree data specify complex cell embeddings of real global unknowns. The separate reality requirements for both actuator blocks are imposed in the compatible-row condition, which this linked declaration does not state.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry

rows.fidelity_note: The temporal frequency is 2ι₂ − ι₁, as in (B.2). The cell and chart references in the sentence concern other linked objects.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime

rows.fidelity_note: The azimuthal frequency is κι₁, as in (B.2). The cell and chart references in the sentence concern other linked objects.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth

rows.fidelity_note: The cell stores the two radial and two vertical endpoints used in the quarter-plane construction surrounding (B.10) and (B.26).
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox

rows.fidelity_note: The linked declaration only lists four chart parameters. The coordinate transformation and the geometric conditions needed to identify them with (B.3) occur in separate definitions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.ChartParams

rows.fidelity_note: The linked data specify a steady profile, forcing, constraints, adjoints and numerical bounds for the fractional setting. The paragraph correctly treats these as general analytic inputs that require further conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.SteadyCert.FracCertData

rows.fidelity_note: The linked data add cell geometry, reference model fields and approximation errors to the steady certificate data. These are the cell inputs described in the paragraph; a representation of the functions still has to be supplied.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.FracCellData

rows.fidelity_note: The quadratic form is the real part of the complex pairing of x with Ax. Its definition imposes no Hermitian or positivity condition on A, as the paragraph warns.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.quadForm

rows.fidelity_note: The expression applies the same quadratic form to the inverse matrix. Interpreting it as a positive weighted squared norm requires separate hypotheses on that matrix.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.inverseWeightedSq

rows.fidelity_note: The polynomial is specified by complex coefficients on a square array of degrees from zero to the chosen degree. The array alone supplies no positivity or geometric interpretation.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly

rows.fidelity_note: A cell is specified by four radial and vertical endpoints. The paragraph correctly assigns positive widths and position in the quarter plane to additional validity conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox

rows.fidelity_note: The cell conditions require 0 ≤ r₁ < r₂ and 0 ≤ z₁ < z₂, exactly the genuine widths and quarter-plane geometry described.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBox

rows.fidelity_note: The mesh supplies finitely many rectangles, resolved, tested and eliminated harmonic sets, and polynomial degrees. The paragraph describes these data together with their separate validity conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh

rows.fidelity_note: The conditions require valid rectangles, overlaps of measure zero, the tested/resolved and eliminated-mode relations, conjugate symmetry and zero azimuthal order on axis cells. These are the mesh properties singled out in the paragraph.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.IsCellMesh

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.SplineJoins
ties.plain: Polynomial joins of a chosen order

rows.fidelity_note: The neighboring polynomial pieces must agree through the prescribed derivative order on every internal radial and polar seam. This is the joined-data requirement described.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.SplineJoins
rows.plain: Polynomial joins of a chosen order

rows.fidelity_note: The two coordinate directions may have different joining orders, and the partition must cover the whole coordinate rectangle. This agrees with the paragraph’s account of joined splines.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJoinedSpline

rows.fidelity_note: An axis of Hermite data specifies breakpoints, the number of endpoint derivatives and the number of interior bubble coefficients. The interpolation formulas are supplied separately.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis

rows.fidelity_note: The scaled Hermite data add node scales and bubble normalisers to the same axis information. This supports the paragraph’s distinction between stored and unscaled coefficients.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetAxis

rows.fidelity_note: The conditions identify the reference field and its chosen second derivatives with those reconstructed from the scaled Hermite data, and identify the forcing modes. The corresponding representations and symmetry conditions remain required.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsScaledJetEntry

rows.fidelity_note: The temporal index associated with ι is 2ι₂ − ι₁, as in (B.2). It is distinct from the azimuthal index.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime

rows.fidelity_note: The azimuthal index associated with ι is κι₁, as in (B.2). The integer κ is the symmetry order.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth

rows.fidelity_note: Reflection sends the lattice label to (−ι₁, ι₂ − ι₁). Under (B.2) this preserves temporal frequency and reverses azimuthal frequency.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip

rows.fidelity_note: Reflection of the physical frequency pair sends (n,m) to (n,−m). This agrees with the paragraph’s distinction between a lattice label and its physical frequencies.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.flipLabel

rows.fidelity_note: An active label belongs to one of the four declared model supports and has a nonzero component somewhere in the cell. Covering the whole union of supports is therefore a sufficient conservative choice.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelLabels
rows.plain: Model harmonics active in a cell

rows.fidelity_note: The condition requires positive period and weight, constant weight, and closure and inclusion properties for the bounding harmonic set. These are the symmetry and parameter-wide parts of the description.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ShapeValuesFacts

rows.fidelity_note: The conditions identify the reference field, its second derivatives away from the exceptional seams, and the forcing fields with their representations. They also require valid shape parameters and harmonic coverage.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsScaledJetEntry

rows.fidelity_note: The linked definition only identifies the exceptional set of axes, joining spheres and spline seams. The assertions about weak derivatives and replacement of second derivatives on that set require the separate regularity results mentioned in the paragraph.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeKnots

rows.fidelity_note: The row data attach each polynomial test to a cell, harmonic, real or imaginary component and weight. This is the raw information used in the orthogonalisation surrounding (B.11).
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues

rows.fidelity_note: The conditions require complete, distinct real row representatives, positive weights, conjugate tests, divergence-free tests, axis conditions and positive definite Gram blocks. They supply the normalisation prerequisites described.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowValues

rows.fidelity_note: The instantiated data must satisfy the row, weight, forcing, pinning and symmetry conditions together. This connects the separately described objects to the same certificate.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsInstanceEntry

rows.fidelity_note: The pinning data supply cell fields and generator representations with their shape parameters and proposed support edges. Compact support, validity and error estimates are imposed separately, as the paragraph indicates.
rows.name: Breakdown.PotentialShape.PinShapeEntry

rows.fidelity_note: The four fields are the two vector potentials, a matrix flux and a scalar pressure correction. With the matrix convention stated, they are the objects used in (B.51) and (B.52).
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialData

rows.fidelity_note: The representation consists of finitely many harmonic keys and the associated potential coefficients. Its regularity is imposed by the separate conditions described in the paragraph.
rows.name: Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotentialSeries

rows.fidelity_note: The conditions control joining, axis behavior and endpoint vanishing for the potentials, flux and pressure. They provide the explicit sufficient representation whose full coefficient format is omitted on p.67.
rows.name: Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialSeries

rows.fidelity_note: The represented potentials and pins must be valid and must equal the fields used in the adjoint estimates. This is the identification required before applying (B.51) and (B.52).
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.PotentialEntriesBounded

rows.fidelity_note: The local Hermitian matrix is measurable and bounded, and its two inequalities hold for every complex gradient and velocity vector. The second inequality excludes the cylindrical axis, matching the stated domain issue.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafValues

rows.fidelity_note: The conditions combine valid harmonic coordinates, local matrix inequalities, model errors, period errors and pressure placement. They express the cell information used before assembling (B.26) and (B.27).
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellCalculusConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The local elimination inequality holds for every vector in the specified admissible set. Positive row weights and the separate zero-slack identity are also required, so checking selected coordinate vectors is insufficient.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The tree data include finite real global coordinates, complex cell embeddings, a distinguished root, pivots and real negative columns. These are the objects used by the matrix-tree argument.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry

rows.fidelity_note: One common family of front matrices must satisfy every node enclosure and the pivot-count condition, with a unique root. This matches the paragraph’s global consistency requirement.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TreeConditionsGiven

rows.fidelity_note: The cell embeddings must match the row representation, the global form must dominate the assembled leaf form, and pressure-head directions must lie in the required kernels. These conditions connect the tree to the actual cell rows.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeRowConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The data include a matrix selecting the retained component and a form for the additional coordinates, with coupling groups and numerical budgets. No orthogonality or idempotence is imposed merely by supplying the selection matrix.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialData

rows.fidelity_note: The retained potential form and the coupling bounds are required on the specified admissible vectors, with all coverage, sign and error conditions. This is the local potential contribution described.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The retained pairing form is bounded by the exact pairing on the same admissible vectors; its unresolved terms have separate Gram and error bounds. This matches the assembly role described.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingConditions

rows.fidelity_note: Used row coordinates are determined by shared real unknowns plus complex gauge and pressure-head terms. Unused and port coordinates remain free complex values, while both actuator blocks are real.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange

rows.fidelity_note: The complete assembly condition joins the potential, pairing, rows, tails, elimination, exterior and tree requirements for the same data. It also makes the required pressure and gauge invariances explicit.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerEntryConditions

rows.fidelity_note: Every omitted harmonic on every cell must be covered by valid regions with sufficient charges, uniformly over the parameter set. A finite list of regions therefore still represents an infinite family of conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsOffModeCover

rows.fidelity_note: For every harmonic, the regions cover the whole exterior, have measurable geometry and overlaps of measure zero, and carry valid pointwise or ray estimates with common charges. The stated exterior obligations remain present.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsExteriorCover

rows.fidelity_note: The far-field enclosures bound the reference strain and the mean and oscillating vorticity gradients at every exterior point, time and angle. They also identify the charges and require a positive common length.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The certificate conditions retain the residual, smallness, inclusion and nontriviality requirements. The pin-target cancellation comes from the specialised profile identities, so it cannot be read from this collection alone.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CertificateClauses

rows.fidelity_note: The reduction data collect the profile, pressure, adjoints, offset expansion, profile-shift bounds and potential data. The final condition requires these choices to agree.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ReductionEntries

rows.fidelity_note: All fifteen conditions are imposed together on the same seven choices of data. This makes the condition the stated starting point for evaluating a candidate.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The profile, pressure and adjoint representations must satisfy their respective identities. The profile identity for the target makes the specialised pin-target gap zero.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.InstantiationBounded

ties.name: Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.VanishesFrom
ties.plain: Zero spline pieces after a cutoff

rows.fidelity_note: For this spline support condition, a missing radial breakpoint is read as 1. It forces an omitted piece to vanish whenever the support threshold is at most 1; the default is part of the condition.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.VanishesFrom
rows.plain: Zero spline pieces after a cutoff

rows.fidelity_note: The conversion uses default node scale 1, default bubble normaliser 0 and default missing breakpoints 0. These are distinct defaults, as the paragraph requires.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetAxis.convert

rows.fidelity_note: The missing-breakpoint default R makes each affected support guard true because R ≤ |R|. A node coefficient needs one guard and a bubble coefficient needs both endpoint guards; when both endpoints are absent, the bubble coefficient is therefore forced to zero.
rows.name: Breakdown.PotentialShape.VanishesBeyond

rows.fidelity_note: A matching node coefficient is multiplied by the inverse scale to the derivative order. A zero scale gives zero for positive orders and one for order zero, agreeing with the stated interpretation.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetAxis.convert

rows.fidelity_note: The scale condition requires only the correct list length and reflection symmetry. It supplies no nonzero or positive lower bound for a node scale.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasSymmetricScale

rows.fidelity_note: The admissible vectors have shared real row parameters, arbitrary complex gauge and pressure-head coefficients, free complex unused and port coordinates, and real actuator coordinates. The full real-linear span is therefore the correct domain for the quadratic test.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelLabels
ties.plain: Model harmonics active in a cell

rows.fidelity_note: The active labels are a filtered subset of the union of the four declared supports. Requiring coverage for that whole union implies coverage for the active subset.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelLabels
rows.plain: Model harmonics active in a cell

rows.fidelity_note: Both coupling-group coverage requirements quantify over the active model labels. Replacing that label set by a containing set makes these particular coverage obligations sufficient, although the other potential conditions still need checking.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The row-group coverage requirement also quantifies over active model labels. Covering the entire declared support is sufficient for this clause, while every row identity and numerical bound remains a separate obligation.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowFunctionalConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The finite expansion requires distinct component, temporal-frequency and azimuthal-order triples, with weights 1/2, 1/2, 1 and denominator (|m|+1/2)². These are exactly the orthogonality and normalisation requirements explained.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalBounded

topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.
topics.name: The fractional extension

topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).
topics.name: The blow-up statements

topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).
topics.name: Passing to the torus

topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).
topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions

topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).
topics.name: Monodromy and the correction

topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).
topics.name: Recurrent profiles

topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).
topics.name: From certificate to profile

topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).
topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate

topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.
topics.name: Encoded cell data

topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).
topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane

topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).
topics.name: Cells, traces and tails

topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).
topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests

topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).
topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound

topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).
topics.name: Changing the profile

topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).
topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error

topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).
topics.name: The offset and the certificate
